provenance.note: Built backward from 2025=100 using year-over-year annual % CPI inflation (World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG), same construction as us.json (index[y] = index[y+1]/(1+inflation[y+1]/100)). 1980-1999, 2001, 2003, 2005-2025 are official World Bank/FRED values. Years 2000, 2002 and 2004 (Japan's deflationary early-2000s period) are ESTIMATED by averaging corroborating secondary series (moneyinrealterms.com and inflationtool.com CPI-index tables) because the primary World Bank series was truncated in the retrieved page for exactly those 3 years; the estimates are consistent in sign and magnitude with the surrounding official deflation readings (-0.7% to -0.9%, ~0.0%).

provenance.note: 1980-2015: IMF/World Bank 'Deposit interest rate' (FR.INR.DPST) annual series for Japan, official. 2016-2025: switched to the Bank of Japan's uncollateralized overnight call-rate policy target (year-end effective rate) because retail deposit-rate series were discontinued/near-zero and would mask the real and economically important feature of this period: the BOJ ran a NEGATIVE policy rate (-0.10%) from Sep 21, 2016 until it ended Negative Interest Rate Policy on Mar 21, 2024, then hiked to 0.25% (Aug 2024), 0.50% (Jan 2025) and 0.75% (Dec 2025). These policy-rate values are used verbatim for 2016-2025 (riskFree and jp_savings are identical, following the same convention as us.json's riskFree/us_savings). This is a deliberate hybrid construction across two related-but-distinct series (bank deposit rate vs. central bank policy rate); treat jp_savings as 'secondary/approximate' for the full history, and especially for 2016-2025 where it represents the policy rate rather than an actual retail savings-account rate (actual retail ordinary/time deposit rates stayed just above zero, ~0.001%-0.03%, even during NIRP, per Bank of Japan deposit-rate statistics at stat-search.boj.or.jp).

provenance.note: Year-end (Dec 31, last trading day) Nikkei 225 closing level, 1980-2025, JPY, price index (no dividend reinvestment). Includes the 1989 bubble peak (38,915.87) and the 1990-1992 crash. Annual % return is the computed year-over-year % change in these closes. All 46 years are sourced directly from the official Nikkei Inc. archive (2021-2025) or well-corroborated secondary aggregators cross-checked against each other and against Wikipedia's 'Nikkei 225' annual-returns table (1980-2020); none interpolated.
